title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes 'ateliers' (workshops) for a combinatorial or tame topology. An atelier has a set of 'figures' F (closed parts), a set M of elementary figures ('magazin', with the incidence relation X ◁ F), orders ≤ (inclusion of closed parts) and ≪ (roughly 'X lies in the interior or open stratum structure of Y'), an operation ∘ (an intersection-type operation), and a dimension or rank |·|. The previous page derived the order ≤ on M from the family of closed sets (X̃ = M_{≤X}) and stated axioms AtM1–AtM5, including the 'compatibility' relation ≍ (a sup exists).

This page first counts axioms. If one starts from the figures with their structure, (F, ≤, ≪, |·|) or (F, M, Δ, ≤, |·|), one needs Mag1–Mag4 (the axioms of a magazin linking ≤, ≪, ∘ on M) plus five further axioms. If one starts from the magazin (M, ≤, ≪, |·|) together with a choice of F, only one supplementary axiom on the choice of F is needed. So the magazin is the economical primary datum, and F is a choice of admissible closed sets.

He calls all of this 'spatial' ateliers. He then opens a parenthesis on 'polyhedral' ateliers, a slight variant.

Definition (after several crossed-out attempts): a magazin M is prepolyideal if, in M, any two elements X, Y that have a common upper bound and a common lower bound have an infimum. Equivalently, each lower set X̃ is 'polyideal' (meets exist inside bounded regions). The crossed-out text hints at a stronger 'polyideal' notion involving finiteness or inductivity of the intervals M_{a≤·≤b}.

For an arbitrary magazin he then introduces a stronger relation ≪_pol:
- X ≪_pol Y iff X ≪ Y and, for every Y' ≤ Y, the induced subfigure X_{Y'} := X̃ ∩ Ouv(Y') is empty or has a largest element, i.e. is itself an elementary figure.
- He notes that X_{Y'} = X∘Y' = Inf^≪(X, Y') in the figure lattice F_M.

Modern reading: this is the passage from regular-CW-like or stratified cell structures, where the intersection of two closed cells is a union of cells, to polyhedral complexes, where the intersection of two closed cells is a single face or empty. The next page shows that prepolyideality is equivalent to X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪_pol Y, and checks that (M, ≤, ≪_pol, |·|) again satisfies Mag1 (transitivity) and Mag2.
errors: No mathematical error on the page; the definitions are in draft and heavily crossed out. The defining clause 'X̃ ∩ Ouv(Y)' should presumably read Ouv(Y'), since the condition is quantified over Y' ≤ Y.
The precise relation between 'prepolyideal' and the crossed-out 'polyideal' (finiteness or inductivity of the intervals M_{a≤·≤b}) is left unsettled on this page.

ideas.what: Counting axioms: the magazin (M, ≤, ≪, |·|) plus one axiom on the choice of F is equivalent to the figure-based presentation with five extra axioms
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of presentations of a cell or stratified structure (face poset versus closed-set lattice)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of face posets and regular CW complexes (Björner 1984 for CW posets)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; the tame-topology program is only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5

ideas.what: Prepolyideal magazin: elements bounded above and below have an inf
ideas.modern_name: Meet condition on face posets / polyhedral complex (intersection of two cells is a cell); locally a meet-semilattice
ideas.usually_credited_to: Polyhedral and abstract polytope combinatorics (Grünbaum, McMullen–Schulte; Björner)

ideas.what: Relation ≪_pol: X ≪ Y and every induced subfigure X∘Y' (Y' ≤ Y) is empty or elementary

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatic 'ateliers' and 'magazins' framework for analysis situs, with a spatial versus polyhedral variant, is an unpublished combinatorial foundation for tame topology. Its comparison with CW posets and abstract polytopes and with o-minimal cell decompositions was never written up. This page itself contains only routine definitions.
missed.quote: Il faut maintenant ouvrir une parenthèse sur les "ateliers polyédraux", qui représentent une variante très légèrement différente.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest: the page documents how Grothendieck intended to axiomatize the stratified or tame spaces sketched in the Esquisse. The mathematics is close to known face-poset theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The definitions correspond to standard combinatorics of polyhedral and regular cell complexes. The interest is historical: an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology framework, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'représentent une [-structure-] {+variante+} un très légèrement différente' → 'représentent une variante très légèrement différente' ('structure' crossed out, 'variante' written above)

'Pas relations plus fortes que / On introduit ... (pas utile, pas même prépolyidéal ...) ≪ (pour tous magazins,' → roughly 'On introduit des relations plus fortes que ≪ (pour tous magazins, pas même prépolyidéaux...)'
'où déf X̃ ∩ Ouv(Y)' likely intended as Ouv(Y')
'(à ti[?] moins ...)' possibly '(à tout le moins...)', uncertain
